newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day mostly up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end choppy day mostly up.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mostly higher after a choppy session spent following the bond market.

Trade for much of the afternoon was very quiet, and a firm Treasury bond futures close lent bullishness to otherwise choppy stock index futures, traders said. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures closed sharply higher after an erratic session in a range from 818.50 to 832.50.
June started the session up the seven-point opening trading limit. After a two-minute trading halt at 0840 CDT/1340 GMT, it extended those gains in brisk trading.
But as Treasury bonds and the dollar sagged, June S&Ps shaved their gains and headed lower, ultimately challenging 818.50 support.
In afternoon trade, bonds recovered and June S&Ps firmed into the close.

"It's a Friday and you have no economic news and a 14-handle range -- it's ridiculous," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "You have to figure it will be pretty volatile until the FOMC meeting," he added.
The Federal Open Market Committee next meets May 20 to consider monetary policy.
Traders tied the early stock and bond bullishness to comments Thursday night by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, which triggered hopes the Fed will leave monetary policy unchanged May 20.

"We think there is enough ambivalence in his speech to suggest that the Fed chairman is willing to see what the next week holds for us with respect to economic news," Evelina Tainer, chief economist with IndoSuez Carr Futures, said in her weekly market directive.
But as the trading session progressed, differing interpretations of the Fed chief's comments flourished.
Some said he had not backed away from a rate rise again in May. Others said bulls have stocks and bonds by the horns and would label even a mixed bag of comments as market-friendly.
Greenspan, in his remarks Thursday night, said he expects economic growth to slow later this year and into next year, but added that the central bank would need to act if that was not the case.

He defended the March 25 rate hike, calling it an insurance policy against future inflation. He acknowledged that there was scant evidence of any imminent resurgence of inflation now, but said the Fed would remain preemptive.
S&P 500 futures traders said Greenspan's remarks set the stage for indecision heading into mid-week inflation data.
"He was successful in his subterfuge," an S&P 500 futures trader said. Another trader predicted that an 810.00 to 840.00 range would prevail into FOMC.

June Nikkei stock index futures ended down in sympathy with the sagging dollar, traders said. June S&P 500 closed up 7.10 points at 829.65, with Midcap 400s up 0.35 at 268.55, Russell up 0.15 at 362.35, Value Lines up 3.50 at 728.00, NYSE Composite up 3.70 pts at 431.70, Nasdaq flat at 925.75, and Nikkei 225 down 525.0 at 19,660.0.
